title: Competencies for 21st Century Learning
before:
What are 21st Century Skills and Competencies?

Culture is changing rapidly for a variety of reasons. Technology is improving at lightening speed and humans are responding almost as quickly. What was extraordinary a decade ago is outdated now. 
In the modern workplace, striking a balance between collaboration and independence is an essential skill. Being nimble problem solvers and adapting strategies is highly valued by many employers. To prepare out students for life as responsible citizens of the world, we need to understand what are the foundations for analytical thinking, creative and practical problem solving, interdependent relationships, and effective communication. 
Exploring 21st Century Skills and Competencies
  • 12 Twenty-first Century Skills from Applied Educational Systems 
  • What Skills are Today's Employers Seeking? from Rasmussen University 
  • Framework for 21st Century Competencies and Student Outcomes from the Singapore Ministry of Education 
  • Life and Career Ready: preparing our students for everything from Maine DOE
Blended or Braided Learning Targets

Modern success requires a weaving together of expertise in several skill areas at once. A business owner must be an expert in the nature of the business and competent in marketing, accounting, personnel management, to name a few. Braided learning targets from across disciplines demonstrate the real-world application that we want students to experience. 

For one example of braiding, click here.

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.
Heading levels skip: jumps h1 to h5. Needs a person.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 2 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "Exploring 21st Century Skills and Competencies" is an h5 with no h4 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 3 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. 1 link sits immediately in front of a colon, where the chevron lands between the term and the punctuation that belongs to it. No word changes and nothing is removed.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: Culture is changing rapidly for a variety of reasons. Technology is improving at lightening speed and humans are responding almost as quickly. What was extraordinary a decade ago is outdated now.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 2 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
